**Warning, experimental features under active development!**

Alignment to V, D, and J gene segments is the critical first step of BCR and TCR analysis. Immcantation supports doing this using IgBlast as part of [Change-O](https://changeo.readthedocs.io/en/stable/examples/igblast.html). However, this setup requires running multiple bash scripts and Python scripts. Instead, we are developing an alternate pipeline that remains within R.

## Download and set up IgBlast executibles

[Download IgBlast binaries here](https://ftp.ncbi.nih.gov/blast/executables/igblast/release/LATEST/). Make sure the version matches your operating system. Move to the directory you want IgBlast to be located and extract the files. The extracted directory location is a critical input to this pipeline.

## Install correct development branch of Dowser

These functions are only available in the `igblast` branch of Dowser.

```{r, eval=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
library(devtools)

install_github("https://github.com/hoehnlab/airrblast")

```

## Download and set up reference database

We can now download the IMGT GENE-DB reference database, and convert it into a search database that IgBlast can use. The commands will create the directories `imgt` and `igblast` and only need to be run once.

These functions are a direct re-coding of the functions in [this setup](https://changeo.readthedocs.io/en/stable/examples/igblast.html)

```{r, eval=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
library(airrblast)

# Location of IgBlast directory
# replace with the name of the directory downloaded
igblast_dir <- "ncbi-igblast-1.22.0"

# Download IMGT GENE-DB int directory "imgt"
# specifying the organism is not necessary, but saves download time
downloadIMGT("imgt", organism="human")

# Set up search databases for IgBlast using imgt database
imgtToIgblast("imgt", "igblast", igblast_dir)
```

## Align BCR sequences to V(D)J references

Here, we align a fasta file of BCR sequences to the IMGT human reference database and add IMGT gaps.

```{r, eval=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
library(dplyr)
library(airr)

data(ExampleFasta)

# make example fasta file
writeFasta(ExampleFasta, "test.fasta")

# Align sequences using IgBlast
data <- assignGenes("test.fasta", 
	igblast=igblast_dir,
	refs="igblast",
	outfile="test.tsv")

# optional, read in output file using AIRR package
data <- airr::read_rearrangement("test.tsv")

# Add IMGT gaps. gapdb is the downloaded imgt reference directory
gapped_data <- addGaps(data, gapdb="imgt", organism="human", locus="Ig")

# remove sequences with missing junctions
gapped_data <- dplyr::filter(gapped_data, !is.na(junction))

# optional, save gapped database using AIRR package
airr::write_rearrangement(gapped_data, "test_gapped.tsv")
```

## Identifying clones, reconstructing germlines, building trees.

From here, you can perform any analyses supported by Immcantation within R. Here, we perform clonal clustering, reconstruct clonal germlines, build trees, and visualize them. These topics are handled in more detail on other pages. In particular:

[Clonal clustering with Scoper](https://scoper.readthedocs.io/en/stable/vignettes/Scoper-Vignette/)
[Building clonal germlines with Dowser](Germlines-Vignette.md)
[Building trees with Dowser](Building-Trees-Vignette.md)
[Plotting trees with Dowser](Plotting-Trees-Vignette.md)

For a full tour, check out the [Immcantation tutorials](https://immcantation.readthedocs.io/en/stable/getting_started/getting-started.html). 

```{r, eval=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}

# note, these next steps use Scoper and Dowser functions
library(scoper)
library(dowser)

# Identify clones using a threshold of 0.1 for convenience
gapped_data <- hierarchicalClones(gapped_data, 0.1, summarize=FALSE)

# read in IMGT database for clonal germline reconstruction
# this is the same directory downloaded above. Isn't that nice?
imgt = readIMGT("imgt/human/vdj")

# reconstruct clonal germlines
gapped_data = createGermlines(gapped_data, imgt, trim_lengths=TRUE)

# formatClones for tree building
clones = formatClones(gapped_data)

# build trees
trees = getTrees(clones, build="pml")

# plot trees
plots <- plotTrees(trees)

# plot largest tree
plots[[1]]

# save all trees as a pdf
treesToPDF(plots, file="trees.pdf")

# save tree objects for later use
saveRDS(trees, "trees.rds")
```
